I’ll create an arrangement of 2n x 2n with these rotations in clockwise order. I see that a Python rotation works by using zip(*[::-1]).     n = len(grid)
    def rotate_cw(a):
        return [list(row) for row in zip(*a[::-1])]
    r90 = rotate_cw(grid)
    r180 = rotate_cw(r90)
    r270 = rotate_cw(r180)
    return [list(grid[i]) + list(r90[i]) for i in range(n)] + [list(r270[i]) + list(r180[i]) for i in range(n)]
